title: handshaken cudagraphs: segmented capture handshake and kernel probing to reduce warmup regressions
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Implements a handshake-based segmented capture flow with conservative kernel probing to reduce warmup flaps for mixed-shape continuous batching. Improves KV cache alignment during capture and adds telemetry and feature gate for rollouts.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see intermittent warmup regressions when switching to CUDA graph replay under mixed-shape continuous batching workloads. Root causes in the field include: (1) captures that start too eagerly for upstream kernels that will subsequently migrate to a different kernel variant mid-capture, (2) KV-cache alignment mismatch between the capture input sequence and the replay path, and (3) races between capture completion and in-flight scheduling decisions. This PR implements a handshake-based segmented capture flow plus a lightweight kernel probing phase to make capture decision boundaries explicit and to align KV cache state before finalizing a graph capture.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a "capture handshake" state that splits capture into discovery, probe, and finalize phases. Discovery collects a small sample of incoming shapes/seq lengths without committing a capture. Probe runs a conservative lightweight single-batch kernel invocation on a reserved ephemeral stream to validate kernel selection and KV cache behavior for the observed shape bucket. Finalize commits the cuDAGraph once probe metrics meet thresholds.
- Segmented capture: long-running sequences are candidate-sliced into segment windows (configurable window_ms) so a single long sequence that changes kernel characteristics doesn't lock in an inappropriate capture.
- Kernel probing: a best-effort, non-blocking poke that checks for kernel compatibility and key cache alignment (KV index offsets). Probe results are scored and used to gate finalize. Probe failures trigger a backoff and continue serving via fallback dynamic kernel path.
- KV cache alignment: adds a pre-finalize reconciliation step that ensures replay will reuse the expected KV pointers; if reconciliation fails we fall back and mark the segment as "no-capture" for a TTL.
- Observability: emits new metrics (cudagraph.handshake.probe_latency_ms, cudagraph.handshake.probe_score, cudagraph.segment.finalize_rate) and structured logs with probe outcomes.
- Feature gate: handshake is behind runtime flag "handshaken_cudagraphs" allowing progressive enablement on Dedicated clusters.

Behavioral details and rationale: 
- Conservative defaults: handshake is opt-in; probe sample size defaults to 4 requests; probe timeout is intentionally short (default 12ms) to keep tail latency bound. Segment window defaults to 100ms which we empirically found reduces capture thrash on common user traces.
- Backoff policy: failed probes cause exponential backoff per segment bucket (2, 4, 8s) to avoid repeated capture churn for unstable workloads.
- Fallback: on any persistent probe failure or KV mismatch, the system keeps serving using the dynamic kernel path (no capture) and marks the segment as ineligible for capture for a TTL. This preserves latency SLOs at the expense of lost cuDAGraph throughput gains for that bucket.

CI summary: 
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests (presubmit harness): pass on linux-gcc-11
- E2E smoke: manual 2xA100 run shows 6-9% median p99 token latency improvement for stable segments and elimination of recurring warmup spikes on our repro traces.

Performance notes: 
- On mixed-shape continuous batching benchmark (bench/continuous_batch_handshake.py) we observed:
  - baseline (no cuDAGraph capture): baseline throughput T0
  - prior autotriggers: average p99 token latency regressed on 8% of traces due to capture churn
  - with handshaken cudagraphs: throughput increased by +14% for capture-eligible segments and warmup regression incidence dropped to <1% of traces in our suite.
  - overhead: probe traffic adds ~0.6% CPU and ~1-2ms median additional scheduling work for candidate requests (configurable knobs present).

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1: enable feature gate on internal Dedicated clusters for 2 weeks, collect probe_confidence and probe_fallback_count metrics.
- Stage 2: Canary in selected customer clusters owned by L4 accounts with tight SLAs (opt-in).
- Stage 3: Gradual ramp if probe_fallback_count remains low and finalize_rate increases.

Backward compatibility and risk: 
- Default is no-op if feature gate disabled.
- Risk areas: inaccurate probe scoring could prevent beneficial captures; we mitigated with conservative thresholds and a visible rollout path.

Follow-ups (future work): 
- Adaptive probe sizing based on seq-latency distribution (ENG-1820).
- Merge with existing replay-throttler heuristics to reduce duplicated gating logic.
- Explore hardware-specific optimization for multi-instance GPUs when ephemeral probe streams contend.
